title: The Vote in Kalsa

situation: Elsin's coalition government is in trouble. Prime Minister Henrik Valde governs with the Highlands Party, a rural party from the north led by Sanna Ekdal, and his majority is thin. Ekdal's voters are angry, and so are the crowds outside parliament.

The opposition is led by Ruben Kask of National Renewal, who says Elsin should decide its own future "without Kordav or the alliance." A government led by Kask would have to decide whether Task Force VEYL stays.
The alliance keeps Valde's office informed about Kordavan activity in a short note each evening, drawn from your brief. Liaison requests go to Kalsa over LATTICE, unless the link is shut.

customer.name: Under Secretary H. Marlowe
customer.wants: Is this Elsin's business, or Kordav's, and what should the alliance do?
customer.context: Her public steps can't be undone, and some quiet ones may not stay quiet.
customer.tipLine: High is public. Medium is quiet. Low changes nothing.

opening.text: Valde's government is in trouble. Tell me whose trouble it is.
opening.reassigned: A new cell, and an old government in trouble. Tell me whose trouble it is.

byTone.good: You were right about the link when nobody wanted you to be. Now Kalsa is wobbling, and everyone in my building has a theory. I'd like yours.
byTone.bad: We got the last one wrong, and Kalsa remembers. This one is about Kalsa. Tell me whose business it is.
byTone.warn: Valde's government is in trouble. Tell me whose trouble it is.

replies.handsoff: I've said we'll work with whoever parliament chooses. Kask's people have asked for a meeting.
replies.handsoff_early: I've said we'll work with whoever parliament chooses. Valde called. He wanted to know when we'd decided he was finished.
replies.channel: The embassy has had coffee with Kask's foreign affairs man. Nothing promised.
replies.postpone: I've asked Valde to postpone. He's thinking about it, which in Kalsa means yes.
replies.restraint: The embassy has asked Elsin's police for restraint. Politely.
replies.warnpub: I've said it in public: Kordav is interfering in Elsin's politics. The press here liked that very much.
replies.warnpriv: Valde has it in tonight's note. He says he'll look into it.
replies.listen: That's a shrug. Kalsa isn't waiting for us.
replies.postponed_next: Valde postponed. The organisers called it an alliance decision, and twice as many came out last night.
replies.backlash: Kask spent the evening on television with my statement. He calls it "the alliance choosing Elsin's government." The Courier agrees with him.
replies.overheard_ksb: KSB led the news with it: "The alliance whispers to Valde that his opponents are Kordav's." It quoted the note.
replies.overheard_police: Valde's police questioned two of the organisers last night, on our warning. They've told the Courier.

groundTruth.state: Ekdal has spent three weeks in her constituency and has decided to leave. Kordav's embassy doubles its press staff to amplify.
The protests grow on their own money. The Bureau posts a forged bank document, meant to be repeated by the alliance and then exposed.
Ekdal leaves. The motion is tabled. The biggest protest, and the only violence.
Ekdal and Kask negotiate. The Bureau posts recycled winter photos of organisers at a Kordavan camp.
The deal is signed. The organisers call off the march.

adversaryPlan.phase: Make the alliance say "Kordav" in public
adversaryPlan.summary: Amplify a fall that would happen anyway, plant evidence that can be debunked, and, if the link is open, feed the alliance its own words.

sources.access: Our embassy's political section in Kalsa
sources.postmortemNote: Accurate, except the walk-up "source close to Valde", who was the Bureau's.

sources.access: Elsin's military intelligence liaison desk. Politics isn't its brief, Kordav is.
The Kalsa Evening Courier, Elsin's biggest paper
sources.postmortemNote: The poll was the most important number in the scenario.

sources.access: A staffer in the Highlands Party. New. Don't task her two days running.

reports.text: The Highlands Party has given Valde a week: a public inquiry into {grievance}, or it leaves the coalition. Ekdal told our political officer she "has not decided anything, and has not been asked to by anyone." {majority} {vell}
reports.postmortemNote: The grievance came from your own record. "Has not been asked to by anyone" was true.

reports.text: About 3,000 people protested outside parliament in Kalsa this afternoon over {grievance}. Peaceful. Many came in by bus from the north.
KSB: "Elsin's people tire of foreign soldiers, and of foreign winters."
{wren}: "Kordav's embassy in Kalsa has doubled its press staff this month and is buying advertising on Elsin's news sites."

Elsin's Ministry of Finance and Economy, which was the Ministry of Finance until last year, regrets that its new letterhead is still delayed. Correspondence on the old paper remains valid until the stock runs out.
reports.postmortemNote: The letterhead. Also the cross-check for R-2-03.

reports.text: Kask and Ekdal met last night for the first time in two years. Both say it was about farm subsidies.
About 12,000 protesters in Kalsa, with tractors from the north. A window was broken at the agriculture ministry. Police made four arrests.
reports.postmortemNote: The protests grew on their own.

reports.text: A "leaked bank document" circulates widely: on the letterhead of Elsin's Ministry of Finance, it records a transfer of 2 million from a Kordavan "Agrarian Fund" to National Renewal.

reveal.tell: The letterhead of the Ministry of Finance, which has been the Ministry of Finance and Economy since last year.

crossCheck.text: The ministry was renamed last year (R-1-05). For one point, C-04 adds an account format Elsin's banks don't use, and an account created on the 26th.

reveal.motive: For the alliance to repeat it, and for Kask to wave the forgery on television the day after.

reports.text: Kask, in an interview: "Elsin's future will be decided in Elsin. Not in Kordav, and not by the alliance."
Last night's alliance note to Valde's office, built from your brief, went {route}. It said: "{kj:1}."
reports.postmortemNote: The note, and the road it took.

reports.text: A source close to Valde's office tells our embassy, unprompted, that {claim:1}.
reports.postmortemNote: Your own judgment, read back to you.

reveal.tell: A source volunteers your own key judgment, in your own words.

crossCheck.text: That wording went to Valde's office last night, over LATTICE (R-2-05).

reveal.motive: Confirmation. It pushes a player who suspects a plot towards saying so in public.

reports.text: A source close to Valde's office says the alliance "has it wrong": Kordav's money is behind the Highlands Party, and Ekdal has been bought.
reports.postmortemNote: An answer to a note it shouldn't have seen.

reveal.tell: The source answers last night's note, which only went to Valde's office.

crossCheck.text: The note crossed LATTICE (R-2-05). HERON (C-01) shows Ekdal decided on her own.

reveal.motive: To change your mind. Kordav wants you at H3.

reports.text: At noon Ekdal took the Highlands Party out of the coalition. A motion of no confidence has been tabled for the morning of the 31st.
reports.postmortemNote: Ekdal left for her own reasons, on her own schedule.

reports.text: The largest protest yet, about 40,000. Police used water cannon near parliament. Thirty people were hurt, two of them police officers.
KSB: "The alliance's man Valde turns water cannon on his own farmers."
{wren}: "Two of the protest's organisers took part in a Kordav-funded youth exchange ten years ago."
Last night's alliance note to Valde's office, built from your brief, went {route}. It said: "{kj:2}."
The same source close to Valde's office says that {claim:2}, and that this is "what everyone in the prime minister's office believes."
reports.postmortemNote: Your own judgment, read back to you.

reveal.tell: Your own key judgment again, word for word.

crossCheck.text: That wording went over LATTICE last night (R-3-05).

reports.text: The same source says Ekdal's press conference "was written in Kordav's embassy."

reveal.tell: The source keeps answering the note.

crossCheck.text: The note crossed LATTICE (R-3-05). HERON (C-01, C-02) shows the decision was Ekdal's.

reports.text: Valde won't resign; he'll face the vote. Kask and Ekdal are close to a deal. Her price is the inquiry and the agriculture ministry.
Photos posted overnight claim to show the protest organisers "at a Kordavan training camp." The men in the photos are in winter coats, and there is snow on the ground behind them.

reveal.tell: Winter coats and snow, in May.
reveal.motive: A public accusation that falls apart within a day is worth more to Kordav than any plot.

reports.text: A poll for the Courier: 58% want a new government. 61% want Task Force VEYL to stay.
reports.postmortemNote: A government falling isn't a country leaving.

reports.text: The embassy's air conditioning has failed in the heat. Kalsa reached 29°C today. Staff may remove their ties.
reports.postmortemNote: The heat. Also the cross-check for R-4-02.

reports.text: Last night's alliance note to Valde's office, built from your brief, went {route}. It said: "{kj:3}."
The same source repeats that {claim:3}, and adds that "the alliance should say so before it's too late."
reports.postmortemNote: Your own judgment, read back to you, with advice.

reveal.tell: Your own words again, now with a recommendation.

crossCheck.text: That wording went over LATTICE last night (R-4-05).

reveal.motive: To get the alliance to speak.

reports.text: The same source says Kordavan money is paying for the protesters' buses.

reveal.tell: The source answers the note again.

crossCheck.text: The note crossed LATTICE (R-4-05). The funding (C-03) is a farmers' union and a transport union.

reports.text: Kask and Ekdal have signed a coalition agreement. Kask, at the signing: "We will review the task force agreement. Review, not end."
KSB: "Tomorrow Elsin chooses: sovereignty, or occupation."
The protest organisers have called off tomorrow's march "to let parliament decide."
Last night's alliance note to Valde's office, built from your brief, went {route}. It said: "{kj:4}."
The same source repeats that {claim:4}, and says the prime minister "is waiting for the alliance to speak."
reports.postmortemNote: Your own judgment, read back to you.

reveal.tell: Your own words, a fourth time.

crossCheck.text: That wording went over LATTICE last night (R-5-04).

reveal.motive: To get the alliance to speak on the last day.

reports.text: The same source says Kask will expel the task force within a month of taking office.

reveal.tell: The source answers the note again.

crossCheck.text: The note crossed LATTICE (R-5-04), and Kask said "review, not end" the same day (R-5-01).

reports.text: HERON: Ekdal decided after three weeks of meetings in her own constituency, where nobody has forgiven anyone. She dislikes Kask, and says she will vote against Valde anyway.
HERON: Ekdal's deal with Kask is the inquiry, the agriculture ministry and a promise not to touch the task force for a year. HERON has seen the draft. Nothing in it mentions Kordav or money.
reports.postmortemNote: A domestic deal that protects the task force.

reports.text: Small donations, a farmers' union and a transport union pay for the buses. One account linked to a Kordavan grain trader gave about a thousandth of the total.
reports.postmortemNote: Real money, and a token Kordavan amount.

reports.text: The letterhead uses the ministry's old name, dropped last year, and an account-number format Elsin's banks don't use. The document was first posted by an account created on the 26th.
Bureau instruction to its Kalsa team: "Amplify. Don't touch the vote; it will fall on its own. What we need is the alliance saying the word Kordav in public."
reports.postmortemNote: The Bureau's plan, in its own words.

reports.text: National Renewal's donors are mostly Elsin businessmen. One is a grain importer who trades with Kordav. Everything is declared.
Elsin's security service: the organisers are local, a farmers' union and a students' group. No foreign links found.
KSB, in passing: "Valde's police now investigate peaceful farmers at the alliance's request."
reports.postmortemNote: The request crossed LATTICE and was used against Valde.

reports.text: With the Highlands Party, Valde survives any motion. Without it, a motion passes.

endings.title: Meddled
endings.text: The motion passes, and Kask's first speech as prime minister is about "the alliance choosing Elsin's government." He asks for the task force to be halved by the autumn.
endings.changedBy: Saying nothing in public about Kordav. The fall was Elsin's own, and the accusation was what Kordav wanted.

endings.title: Postponed
endings.text: The vote happens a week late, after a week of riots blamed on the alliance. Kask wins it by more than he would have.
endings.changedBy: Letting parliament vote. The street was standing down by the last day.

endings.title: Overheard
endings.text: Kask governs with a grudge, and Valde's last week is remembered as a hunt for a plot that wasn't there.
endings.changedBy: Not warning Valde about a plot that wasn't there. A private warning doesn't stay private when someone else is reading the note.

endings.title: Hands off
endings.text: The motion passes. Kask's first call is to the embassy. The task force agreement is reviewed over the summer, and survives with a new name.

endings.title: Kept out of it
endings.text: The motion passes. Kask's government is polite and distant, and the review takes a year.
endings.changedBy: A quiet channel to the opposition before the last day, and a public commitment to respect the vote once the coalition had broken.

dailyUpdates.text: A confidence motion against Valde's government is being talked about in the corridors. Nothing has been tabled.
Ekdal has called a press conference for noon.
The vote is two days away.

script.text: The Highlands Party gave Valde a week over a grievance its voters had carried all year. Kordav's embassy hired more press officers.
Kask and Ekdal talked. A bank document appeared on a letterhead that hasn't existed since last year.
Ekdal left the coalition. Forty thousand people came out, and the police used water cannon.
Photos of organisers at a Kordavan camp showed snow, on a 29-degree day. Most of Elsin wanted a new government and the same task force.
Ekdal and Kask signed. The march was called off.

lessons: Not everything bad is the adversary's doing. Sometimes it's just a coalition.
An adversary can want to be accused. Ask who gains from your statement, not only from the event.
Your own assessment, quoted back to you by someone who shouldn't have read it, isn't corroboration. It's a leak.
A government falling isn't a country leaving.
Hands off isn't the same as eyes shut.

analysts.name: Imre Vasko
analysts.reveal: Anchors on his first theory. After the damage assessment he saw Kordav in everything. Right once, about the cancelled march.

analysts.name: Noor Halden
analysts.reveal: Slow but careful. Never wrong. The letterhead and the snow, each a day late.

analysts.name: Tess Marrow
analysts.reveal: She reads crowds and polls, and was right every time. Her best scenario.

notes.text: Three thousand on a weekday is real anger. Nobody pays people to stand in the rain for that.
Doubling the press staff is how it starts.
Kask's line is anti-everyone. Kordav won't like that as much as it thinks it does.
The letterhead says Ministry of Finance. It hasn't been called that since last year.
Ten years ago. They plan long.
A youth exchange ten years ago isn't a recruitment.
Sixty-one percent want the task force to stay. That's the number.
There's snow on the ground in that photo. It's May.
If they're calling off the march, they think they've already won in parliament.
